extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent attorneys/agents, IP practitioners, and USPTO personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and proposed amendments governing the content, effect, tying, withdrawal, and enforcement conditions of statutory and terminal disclaimers filed to obviate nonstatutory (obviousness-type) double patenting before the USPTO. Includes definitions (direct/indirect tying, final invalidity), procedural/form requirements, and alternatives to filing a terminal disclaimer with the proposed agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability standard (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. law, a person is entitled to a patent, absent certain exceptions, for an invention that is new and not obvious as of the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background explanation of why continuing applications and follow-on patents with effectively the same filing date can give rise to patents claiming obvious variants of an invention; sets context for nonstatutory double patenting doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of obviousness-type (nonstatutory) double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the doctrine of obviousness-type double patenting, the USPTO rejects patentably indistinct claims when the subject applications/patents and the applications/patents whose claims form the basis of the nonstatutory double patenting: (1) have the same inventive entity, at least one common (joint) inventor, a common applicant, and/or a common owner/assignee; or (2) are not commonly owned but are owned by parties to a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why obvious variants across same or different patent families may create nonstatutory double patenting rejections and motivates the use of terminal disclaimers to obviate such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a terminal disclaimer (current practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer will ensure that the term of the patent with the terminal disclaimer will not extend beyond the term of the patent forming the basis of the nonstatutory double patenting, and its enforcement provision prevents harassment of an alleged infringer by multiple parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the current protective function of terminal disclaimers (term alignment and enforcement limitations) and how multiple patents tied by disclaimers nonetheless can deter competition because challengers may have to invalidate each patent separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer recording requirements (§1.321(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee disclaiming any complete claim(s) or dedicating term must ensure the disclaimer: (1) is signed by the patentee or an attorney/agent of record; (2) identifies the patent and complete claim(s) or term being disclaimed; (3) states the present extent of the disclaimant’s ownership interest; and (4) is accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of the disclaimer is published in the Official Gazette and attached to printed copies of the specification; the disclaimer is binding on the disclaimant and successors/assigns and must be recorded in the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer basic filing requirements (§1.321(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed by an applicant must: (1) for applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, be signed by the applicant or attorney/agent of record; for applications filed before that date, signature rules vary depending on assignee/interest; (2) specify the portion of the term being disclaimed; (3) state the present extent of the disclaimant’s ownership interest in the patent to be granted; and (4) be accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies different signature/authority rules depending on filing date and ownership interest; applies whether filed in an application, a patent, or a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement condition for terminal disclaimers filed to obviate nonstatutory double patenting (§1.321(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate nonstatutory double patenting must include an agreement that the subject patent (or any patent granted on its application) shall be enforceable: (i) only for and during such period that it is commonly owned with the reference patent (or any patent granted on the reference application); and (ii) only if the subject patent is not tied and has never been tied directly or indirectly to a patent by one or more terminal disclaimers filed to obviate nonstatutory double patenting in which: (A) a claim has been finally held unpatentable or invalid under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 by a Federal court or at the USPTO with all appeals exhausted; or (B) a statutory disclaimer of a claim is filed after any challenge based on 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 to that claim has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposed additional enforcement agreement is voluntary in the sense it is part of the terminal disclaimer language required for issuance; it does not adjudicate claim validity but conditions enforceability to reduce the burden on challengers who otherwise might need to invalidate multiple tied patents. The terminal disclaimer remains unidirectional (binds only the patent where it is filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enforcement/waiver provision for joint research agreement exceptions (§1.321(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the reference patent/application is not commonly owned but was disqualified as prior art because of a joint research agreement, the terminal disclaimer must: (1) comply with b(2)–(4); (2) include signatures as required; and (3) include a provision waiving the right to separately enforce the subject patent and the reference patent and agreeing the subject patent shall be enforceable: (i) only while the subject patent and the reference patent are not separately enforced; and (ii) only if the subject patent is not tied and has never been tied directly or indirectly to a patent by one or more terminal disclaimers filed to obviate nonstatutory double patenting in which (A) a claim has been finally held unpatentable/invalid under 102/103 with appeals exhausted; or (B) a statutory disclaimer of a claim is filed after any challenge under 102/103 to that claim has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph tailors the enforcement limitation to cases where the reference was excepted from prior-art status under joint research agreement rules, requiring an express waiver of separate enforcement in addition to the tying/invalidity conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of direct tying
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject patent is tied directly by a terminal disclaimer to another patent when: (1) the terminal disclaimer is filed in the subject patent or application; and (2) the other patent (or its issuing application) is the reference patent or application identified in that terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tying by a terminal disclaimer is unidirectional — the terminal disclaimer ties the subject patent only, not the reference patent. Direct tying is illustrated in Example 1 (W ← X). Recorded terminal disclaimers filed before issuance may be withdrawn; if withdrawn before issue, the patent was never tied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of indirect tying (by two or more terminal disclaimers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject patent is tied indirectly to another patent when: (1) a terminal disclaimer filed in the subject identifies an intermediate patent/application as the reference; and (2) a terminal disclaimer filed in that intermediate identifies the other patent (or its application) as the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect tying can propagate through chains of terminal disclaimers (examples 2 and 3: W ← X ← Y ← Z). Withdrawal of terminal disclaimers in intermediate applications can undo indirect tying depending on timing (detailed four illustrations). Examples explain effects if disclaimers are withdrawn before/after patent issuance of subject/intermediate/other patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal rules for terminal disclaimers and effect on tying
rubrics_metrics.description: A recorded terminal disclaimer may be withdrawn if timely requested before the application in which it is filed issues as a patent, or before a reexamination certificate issues; after a patent or reexamination certificate issues, a recorded terminal disclaimer will not be nullified. If withdrawn before issuance, the patent granted was never tied to the identified patent/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For disclaimers filed in patents, the recorded terminal disclaimer is considered part of the original patent (35 U.S.C. 253(b); 37 CFR 1.321(a)). For reexamination, a terminal disclaimer is a proposed amendment that does not take effect until the reexamination certificate issues. Examples throughout the preamble illustrate practical consequences of withdrawal timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'a claim has been finally held unpatentable or invalid'
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Finally held unpatentable’ refers to a final determination by the USPTO in an AIA trial or a reexamination proceeding that one or more claims are unpatentable after all appeals or appeal rights are exhausted; ‘finally held . . . invalid’ relates to a final decision entered in a Federal court in a civil action holding one or more claims invalid after all appeals or appeal rights are exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition establishes the trigger condition for the proposed enforceability-limiting agreement in terminal disclaimers (i.e., when tied patents become unenforceable because a tied patent’s claim was finally invalidated over prior art). The proposed agreement cannot be avoided by filing a statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) after a 102/103 challenge has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed terminal disclaimer is not an admission of obviousness or requirement to stipulate patentable indistinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO opted not to propose a rule requiring a stipulation that the claims are not patentably distinct, and the proposed rule does not require treating filing a terminal disclaimer as an admission of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains comments received for and against treating terminal disclaimers as admissions; cites case law (e.g., SimpleAir, Motionless Keyboard, Ortho Pharm., Quad Envtl.) that filing a terminal disclaimer is not an admission on the merits. The proposed agreement conditions enforceability but 'does not concern the validity of claims.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical alternatives to filing a terminal disclaimer with the proposed agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants facing a nonstatutory double patenting rejection may avoid filing a terminal disclaimer with the proposed agreement by: (1) combining the conflicting claims into a single application; (2) canceling or amending conflicting claims in the application or the other application; (3) arguing that rejected claims are patentably distinct from the claims of the reference patent/application; or (4) filing a reissue application of the patent whose claims formed the basis to add canceled conflicting claims (provided no new matter is introduced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may also separate patentably distinct claims into another application and file a terminal disclaimer with the proposed agreement only in the application having indistinct claims. If claims are amended after filing a terminal disclaimer so they no longer conflict, an applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to withdraw the terminal disclaimer prior to issuance to avoid the proposed agreement’s effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and ownership proof rules (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory rules differ by context: patents (a)(1) require signature by the patentee or attorney/agent of record; applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 require signature by applicant or attorney/agent of record; applications filed before that date may require signatures by applicant and/or assignee depending on recorded interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers and statutory disclaimers must 'state the present extent of the disclaimant’s ownership interest' and meet signature requirements to be recorded. The rule enumerates these variations to ensure the PTO can record disclaimers properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording/Publication and permanence after issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded terminal disclaimers filed in a patent are considered part of the original patent and a notice of the disclaimer is published in the Official Gazette and attached to printed copies of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a terminal disclaimer is recorded in an issued patent it will not be nullified; implications differ for disclaimers in reexamination or pre-issuance applications where withdrawal before issuance can avoid tying effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection / PRA / forms impacted
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule modifies terminal disclaimers and proposes a new information collection (OMB control number 0651–NEW) to reflect the updated requirements and estimates for burdens. Impacted forms include PTO/AIA/25, PTO/SB/25, PTO/SB/25a, PTO/AIA/26, PTO/SB/26, PTO/SB/26a, PTO/AIA/63, PTO/SB/63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble provides estimated changes in respondent counts, burden hours, and filing fees and solicits public comment on the PRA collection. The USPTO estimates ~20% of applicants may opt not to file terminal disclaimers containing the proposed agreement initially, and accounts for decreased filings in burden estimates.
